NOT A GATE -- R5's question asked again INSIDE the shortlist, added because a shortlist
that improves the ranking has not shown that the WALK improves it. Same candidate sets,

inside the shortlist the walk DOES beat counting. The shortlist and the walk are doing different jobs: the shortlist removes the hubs the degree column was riding on, and once they are gone the structure is what is left.
the REM shortlist earns its place: narrowing the candidate set by connectivity or compartment improves the ranking, not just the runtime.
Stoichiometric coefficients are dropped: this is topology, not flux, so nothing here
says a proposed step is mass-balanced or thermodynamically allowed.
One reaction is ablated at a time, so a gap that needs two reactions is invisible.
Recovering a reaction Human-GEM already contains is not the same as proposing one it
does not. Every held-out reaction was curated INTO the model by somebody; a genuinely
missing step has no such guarantee and that difference is not measured here.
Compartment membership comes from the SBML, not from an independent assay.
